text: A Problem moves into a Known Error state the moment its root cause is identified — root_cause and cause_notes confirmed — but a permanent fix hasn't been built, tested, or deployed yet. It's a distinct middle condition: neither still investigating, nor actually fixed.

Without a Known Error mechanism, every new Incident matching an already-diagnosed problem forces the agent to either re-investigate from scratch or escalate and wait, even though the cause and a workaround are already documented somewhere in the system. Flagging the Problem as a Known Error, with the workaround written clearly, solves exactly that — the next agent doesn't need the whole investigation, just the workaround, fast.

That value only exists if agents can actually find the record when a similar Incident comes in. In a mature implementation, Known Error records get surfaced through Knowledge Management — often by generating a knowledge article straight from the Problem record, so the workaround shows up in the same search agents already use for anything else. Chapter 5 covers that mechanism in full.

A Known Error that only lives inside the Problem table, invisible to search, delivers almost none of its intended value. The entire point of the state is putting a workaround in front of the next agent before they start investigating something already understood.

It's worth being explicit: flagging Known Error and documenting a workaround does not resolve the Problem. The underlying cause is still present in the environment. It's a holding state that prevents redundant investigations while the real fix — eventually recorded in fix_notes — is still being built.

Closing a Problem the moment a workaround exists, instead of waiting for a real permanent fix, is exactly the kind of shortcut that lets a real cause quietly linger for months. Next, we put all three Problem lessons together in a worked lab scenario.
